verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: After you come into the land I am giving you as your home,

you will bring gifts made by fire to the LORD from your cattle or your flocks. It may be a burnt offering or another sacrifice, to keep a special promise, or as a freely given gift, or at your special feasts, as a smell that pleases the LORD.
Whoever brings his offering must also bring the LORD a grain offering of about one and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with about one litre of olive oil.
With each lamb for the burnt offering or other sacrifice, also prepare about one litre of wine as a drink offering.
With a ram, prepare a grain offering of about three kilograms of fine flour mixed with about one and a third litres of oil,
and about one and a third litres of wine as a drink offering. It will be a smell that pleases the LORD.
When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or other sacrifice, to keep a special promise or as a peace offering to the LORD,
bring with the bull a grain offering of about four and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with about two litres of oil.
Also bring about two litres of wine as a drink offering. It will be a gift made by fire, a smell that pleases the LORD.
This is what must be done for each bull, each ram, and each lamb or young goat.
Do this for each animal, however many you prepare.
Everyone born in the land must do these things in this way when bringing a gift made by fire, a smell that pleases the LORD.
If a foreigner is living among you, or anyone else who lives with you in the years to come, and he wants to bring a gift made by fire with a smell that pleases the LORD, he must do just as you do.
The community must have one rule for you and for the foreigner living among you. It is a rule forever for all your families to come. Foreigners and you are the same before the LORD.
The same laws and rules apply to you and to the foreigner living among you."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you come into the land where I am taking you,
and you eat the food of the land, set some of it aside as a special gift to the LORD.
From the first of your dough, give a loaf as a special gift. Give it just as you give a special gift from the grain at the threshing place.
For all time to come, you must give the LORD a special gift from the first of your dough.
You may make a mistake and fail to keep some of these commands the LORD gave Moses,
any of the commands the LORD gave you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave them and on through all time to come.

If the whole community did this by mistake, without knowing it, the whole community must offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a smell that pleases the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering as the rules say, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest will make the whole community of Israel right with God, and they will be forgiven, because it was a mistake. They have brought the LORD their gift made by fire and their sin offering for their mistake.
The whole community of Israel will be forgiven, and so will the foreigners living among them, because all the people were part of the mistake.
If one person sins by mistake, he must bring a one-year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest will make that person right with God before the LORD for the sin he did by mistake. When he has been made right with God, he will be forgiven.
The same rule applies to everyone who sins by mistake, whether born in Israel or a foreigner living among them.
But anyone who sins on purpose, in open defiance, whether born in the land or a foreigner, insults the LORD. That person must be cut off from his people.
He has treated the LORD's word with contempt and broken his command. That person must surely be cut off. His guilt stays on him."
While the people of Israel were in the desert, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community.
They kept him under guard, because it was not yet clear what should be done to him.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "The man must be put to death. The whole community must stone him outside the camp."
So the whole community took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: For all time to come, you must make tassels on the corners of your clothes, with a blue cord on each tassel.

These tassels will help you remember. When you see them, you will remember all the commands of the LORD and obey them. Then you will not follow the desires of your own heart and eyes, which lead you to be unfaithful to me.
So you will remember and obey all my commands, and you will be holy to your God.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God."
